description: Spring's annotation-based layer, enabled with @EnableCaching, that stores method results in a provider such as Caffeine or Redis.
Removing or updating cached entries when the data changes, with @CacheEvict or @CachePut, plus a time to live as a safety net.
The maximum time an entry may stay in a cache before it expires, which bounds how stale a value can be.
A response header that identifies a version of a resource so a client can revalidate it and receive 304 Not Modified.
A header whose max-age sets response freshness and whose public or private directives control shared-cache reuse.
A rate limiting algorithm where requests take tokens from a bucket that refills at a steady rate, allowing bursts up to its size.
The status a server returns when a client exceeds its rate limit, optionally with a Retry-After header.
Applying rate limits in a proxy, load balancer or gateway so excess traffic is refused before it reaches the application.
